LESSON: PHONOLOGICAL AWARENESS

Grade: Grade 1
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES
Strand: SPEAKING
Topic 2.3: Phonological Awareness

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Phonological Awareness. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. blend given letter sounds to make syllables and syllables to form words
2. segment syllables to letter sounds and words to syllables
3. appreciate word formation by actively engaging in blending and segmenting letter sounds and syllables my home, my community) Core-Competence to be developed: Communication and collaboration: learners work in pairs and groups to sound words Critical thinking and problem solving: learners blend and segment words

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. blend given letter sounds to make syllables and syllables to form words
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to blend given letter sounds to make syllables and syllables to form words. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

2. segment syllables to letter sounds and words to syllables
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to segment syllables to letter sounds and words to syllables. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

3. appreciate word formation by actively engaging in blending and segmenting letter sounds and syllables my home, my community) Core-Competence to be developed: Communication and collaboration: learners work in pairs and groups to sound words Critical thinking and problem solving: learners blend and segment words
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to appreciate word formation by actively engaging in blending and segmenting letter sounds and syllables my home, my community) Core-Competence to be developed: Communication and collaboration: learners work in pairs and groups to sound words Critical thinking and problem solving: learners blend and segment words. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: When you meet your teacher in the morning, say “Good morning” clearly and smile.

Example 2: Listen to a short story about a child walking to school. Then tell a friend one thing that happened.

Example 3: Write three sentences about your school using new words from this lesson.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Phonological Awareness.
2. Explain Phonological Awareness to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Phonological Awareness.
4. Show that you can: blend given letter sounds to make syllables and syllables to form words
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Phonological Awareness. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: Why is Phonological Awareness important to you?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 8: REMEMBER

1. blend given letter sounds to make syllables and syllables to form words
2. segment syllables to letter sounds and words to syllables
3. appreciate word formation by actively engaging in blending and segmenting letter sounds and syllables my home, my community) Core-Competence to be developed: Communication and collaboration: learners work in pairs and groups to sound words Critical thinking and problem solving: learners blend and segment words

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Learner lesson
